subject: Escalation: Stratos Capital — MFN & Exclusivity Requests (exec review)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Escalation: Stratos Capital — MFN & Exclusivity Requests (exec review)

Team,

I need an executive decision on the Stratos opportunity — we hit a set of non-standard, high-risk commercial asks in the latest redline from their GC that go beyond the playbook. Key items:

- MFN: they want an MFN clause tying our pricing to any competitor pricing they secure during the term (no carve-outs).
- Benchmark/SLA incentives: a tiered benchmark clause that would trigger hefty credits if latency/availability falls below a sliding scale (they want uncapped credits tied to revenue).
- Exclusivity: a 12-month exclusivity for our product integration in APAC (broad language that reads like a de facto market exclusivity).
- Audit/access: requests for quarterly audits and access to internal performance traces and logs.

Financials: the deal is ~ $3.2M ARR with a 3-year commitment. They've pushed for a 30% list discount in exchange for exclusivity; RevOps modeled that at ~22% DSCR impact to target revenue in APAC. Legal flagged the MFN and sweeping exclusivity as unacceptable without significant carve-outs.

Attachments: attached redline (Stratos_SOW_v3_redline.pdf) and our one-pager (deal_summary_Stratos.xlsx).

Ask: Exec guidance on the following — please reply with APPROVE / ADJUST / DENY for each line and any suggested counter-language:
  1) Allow MFN limited to published list pricing / same scope only? (we should not be bound to competitor private discounts)
  2) Exclusivity: allow a 6-month technical-integration exclusivity limited to the Stratos integration (not company-level)?
  3) Discount: legal/RevOps recommend cap at 20% with performance-based rebates (not large up-front). Can we approve up to 30% for strategic carve-outs?

Given the size, we can escalate to Jonas/leadership for final sign-off but I want to surface trade-offs now.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Escalation: Stratos Capital — MFN & Exclusivity Requests (exec review)

Rishi — thanks for the clear summary. My take:

1) MFN: absolutely needs to be scoped. Proposed language: MFN limited to publicly posted, third-party list prices for identical SKU/scope, expressly excluding privately negotiated discounts, promotional campaigns, and partner-only pricing. If we accept, add a sunset (12 months) and a floor (we retain right to offer one-time promotional credits).

2) Exclusivity: we can offer a narrowly scoped technical integration exclusivity (APAC) for 6 months tied to specific product modules (Search API v2). No company-wide market exclusivity. Put a performance milestone: if we miss onboarding deadlines, exclusivity voids.

3) Discount: counter with 18% standard discount + a success-based rebate (up to additional 7% paid quarterly if ARR milestones hit). Approve up to 25% only if execs accept both the MFN carve-outs above and a timeboxed exclusivity. 30% requires Legal/Risk to accept MFN + exclusivity limits and Sales to commit to strict non-recurring credits cap.

I've attached a tracked-changes PDF with suggested edits to MFN/exclusivity language. I think we can close this if we hold firm on MFN carve-outs and cap the credit exposure.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Escalation: Stratos Capital — MFN & Exclusivity Requests (exec review)

Team,

Legal review notes (high level):

- MFN: we can accept a narrowly scoped MFN that references only publicly available list/pricing for identical products and explicitly excludes privately negotiated or volume-based discounts and partner-only promotions. We need a definite definition of "identical scope" (same SKU, seat count, term). Add a 12-month sunset on MFN and a written notice + cure period before any price parity obligation kicks in. No retroactive price adjustments.

- Exclusivity: cannot accept a blanket 12-month market exclusivity. Approve only a 6-month limited exclusivity tied to a named integration/module and specific APAC accounts. Include termination triggers (missed milestones) and carve-outs for channel/partner deals.

- Benchmarks/credits: we will not accept uncapped revenue-based credits. Propose a service credit schedule capped at 2% of annual contract value per incident and an annual cap at 6% of ARR for their account. Any additional remediation must be handled through a service-level remediation plan, not direct revenue clawback.

- Audit/access: provide certs (SOC2, ISO) and access to aggregated performance metrics. Deny on-demand deep internal trace access and prevent access to raw logs or PII. For onsite audits, require redacted reports and an executed NDA plus paid audit fees.

Trade-off recommendation for Execs: authorize commercial team to offer up to a 20% discount + the 6-month technical exclusivity + the MFN limited as described. Alternatively, authorize up to 25% only if Execs accept increasing the credit cap to 4%/yr and a firm limit on audit scope. Do NOT approve 30% discount with broad MFN/exclusivity.

If leadership wants to prefer market share over near-term margin for a flagship anchor customer, that's a strategic call — we should route it to Jonas for final sign-off.

Sofia Ivanova
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

Jonas — forwarding the thread. Key options for an exec decision:

A) Approve (recommended): 20% discount + limited MFN (public list prices only, 12-month sunset) + 6-month integration exclusivity (APAC, module-limited) + 2%/incident credit cap, annual 6% cap.

B) Strategic concession: 25% discount + same MFN/exclusivity but raise annual credit cap to 4% — acceptable only if leadership signs off on incremental margin hit and RevOps accepts model.

C) Reject broad asks: refuse MFN and exclusivity; move to standard terms and walk if needed.

Please reply with the option you want to pursue. If you prefer, I can schedule a 20-minute call.

Thanks,
Rishi
